summary: Iteration 11 verifies the boundary fix in POST /api/auth/login and cleans up leftover TEST_* data. critical_code_review_comments: auth_routes.py::login() now correctly raises 429 immediately when count >= MAX_ATTEMPTS after find_one_and_update, fixing the iter10 off-by-one. Lockout message on 5th failure is user-facing and clear.
change_password guards with `if user.get('phone')` before deleting the lock key — safe.
client_ip() reads X-Forwarded-For only for storage/logging, not as a rate-limit key. Documented in lock_key() docstring.

rca of the issue: Iter10 reported an off-by-one where the 5th wrong login returned 401 with an empty 'Sisa' suffix instead of 429. Main agent fixed by moving the lockout branch to right after the counter increment: if the newly incremented count >= MAX_ATTEMPTS, raise HTTP 429 with the 15-menit lockout message instead of falling through to the 401 'Sisa N' branch. Verified in iter11 with the strict test_progressive_then_429 case (attempts 5 and 6 both 429) and via the frontend toast on attempt 5.
